definition: Passive learning is a way of learning in which students mainly receive material rather than actively use language skills. In this source, it refers to instruction centered on learning the alphabet instead of more active work on listening and speaking.

reasons: The definition adds an unsupported general meaning for “passive learning” (“students mainly receive material rather than actively use language skills”); the source only says language teaching had been focused on the passive learning of the alphabet.
The source supports a contrast with listening and speaking, but it does not define passive learning itself as that broader instructional mode.

The packet supports that “language teaching has been focused on the passive learning of the alphabet,” but it does not define passive learning in general as students mainly “receive material rather than actively use language skills.”

The packet mentions that research on teaching listening and speaking skills was limited, which is related to the comparison, but it does not explicitly state the full framing that the alphabet-centered instruction is “instead of more active work on listening and speaking” as a definition of passive learning.
